findings.section: Root cause (Mechanism bullet 1) and Prototype review finding #1
findings.problem: The startup control flow described for the reporter's exact scenario is wrong. The report says runDesktopApp runs `await applyServerTarget(); connectServerSync.syncNow()` and that the last menu build is refreshApplicationMenu() at main.ts:1235 before syncNow at 2288 sets the reason. But for an unreachable custom URL, applyServerTarget's `await loadWindowUrl({url: target.url})` (main.ts:1229) rejects (BrowserWindow.loadURL rejects with ERR_FAILED/ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED; loadUrlIntoWindow only swallows ERR_ABORTED), so neither the refresh at 1235, startRemoteSystemConfigSync at 1233, nor syncNow at 2288 ever run; the promise unwinds to the runDesktopApp catch which shows the 'Could not open bb' error screen. The reporter's own #1494 (which the report cites) documents exactly this. The first sync in that scenario happens only when the user opens Window>Server (menu-will-show -> onListRequested, main.ts:757-761). The report's conclusions (silent null, prototype note would not show at first open) still hold — arguably more strongly — but the cited evidence/line ordering is inaccurate and the report states 'high confidence' in it.
findings.evidence: apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1226-1235 (custom branch: bbAppLoaded=true; await loadWindowUrl; startRemoteSystemConfigSync; refreshApplicationMenu), desktop-window-factory.ts:197-210 (rethrows non-ERR_ABORTED), main.ts:2292-2301 (catch -> loadStartupError). Issue #1494 body: 'refreshApplicationMenu() at the end of applyServerTarget() never runs'.
findings.fix: Rewrite the mechanism bullet: in the reporter's flow the startup sync never runs because applyServerTarget rejects; the sync first runs from onServerMenuWillShow while the popup is already built, and a skipped sync never rebuilds the menu. Update the prototype review's cited lines accordingly (menu built at main.ts:2272 / menu-will-show at 757-761 rather than 1235 vs 2288).

findings.problem: The failing assertion in test 1 (`expect(Object.keys(sync)).toContain('getSkipReason')`) asserts the reporter's prototype API name rather than an observable bug; it would still fail against a valid fix that uses a callback (which is what the report's own proposed fix recommends). The bug itself is documented by the passing assertions plus test 2.
findings.evidence: issue-1753-repro.test.ts:62; report's proposed fix suggests onSkipped(reason)/onSyncResult, not getSkipReason.
findings.fix: Either drop the accessor-name assertion and let test 2 be the failing repro, or state explicitly that assertion 1 encodes one possible remedy and is expected to be replaced by whichever fix lands.

findings.problem: Prerequisites are not stated: run.sh needs `xvfb-run` (Xvfb) installed and build.sh needs esbuild resolvable from apps/desktop; build.sh also overwrites menu.bundle.js inside the repro artifact directory in place. A clueless reader on a machine without Xvfb gets an unexplained failure.
findings.evidence: run.sh calls xvfb-run -a; build.sh calls pnpm exec esbuild; running build.sh rewrote /tmp/bb-reports/issues/1753/repro/menu-shot/menu.bundle.js (byte-identical in my run).
findings.fix: Add a one-line prerequisites note (Linux with xvfb-run; esbuild comes from the desktop package deps) and mention the bundle is regenerated in place.
